subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should OpenClaw resolve the remaining Slack latency gap by documenting HTTP Request URLs as the preferred low-latency hosted transport, or by changing Slack setup/default behavior beyond the existing `mode: "http"` support?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists and Slack's own guidance favors HTTP for deployed apps, but stronger OpenClaw guidance or defaults would change setup expectations and public-ingress requirements for users.

options.title: Document hosted HTTP mode as preferred
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default local/private path and make Slack docs/setup guidance explicitly prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where latency matters.

options.title: Sponsor a setup/default change
options.body: Have maintainers choose a stronger onboarding or default change for new hosted Slack installs, with fresh-install and upgrade/operator proof before implementation.

options.title: Accept current transport table
options.body: Decide the existing docs are sufficient and close only after recording that no additional latency-specific guidance is planned.

recommendation.title: Document hosted HTTP mode as preferred
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default local/private path and make Slack docs/setup guidance explicitly prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where latency matters.

likelyOwner.reason: They produced the latency decomposition, merged the current-main partial fixes, and scoped the remaining follow-up to HTTP-mode guidance.
